## Highlights

**coyotenote is now one app: the web app.** The terminal app is gone, and the binary is called `coyotenote`. This release adds quick open, an outline, images, note history, properties and tags, and opens in your browser when it starts.

Your notes stay where they were: the default vault is still `~/.local/share/coyotenote-web`. If you used the terminal app's vault (`~/.local/share/coyotenote`), open it with `coyotenote ~/.local/share/coyotenote`.

## New

- **Quick open** (Ctrl/⌘+K): jump to a note by typing a few letters of its path. Start with `#` to jump to a heading, or `>` to run a command. Anything you type can also become a content search or a new note. Searching note contents moves to Alt+S or Ctrl/⌘+Shift+E.
- **Outline** (Alt+O): the open note's headings beside the text. Click one to jump to it; the outline marks the section you are reading.
- **Folders** in the sidebar collapse, and you can **drag a note** onto a folder to move it. Links follow, as they do for a rename.
- **Images:** paste, drop or pick an image, and it is saved in the vault's `attachments/` folder and linked with plain Markdown. Write and Preview show vault images, including `![[embeds]]` in Preview. Remote images are still never fetched.
- **Note history:** coyotenote keeps earlier versions of each note in the vault's hidden `.history/` folder. It keeps one at most every 10 minutes while you type, and always when the file was changed outside the app. The history dialog shows what changed and restores any version.
- **Properties:** notes with YAML or TOML front matter now open in Write, with the front matter in an editable Properties box. Untouched front matter is saved exactly as it was.
- **Tags** from front matter and `#tags` in the text. A menu under the search box filters the note list by tag; tags in Preview are clickable.
- The app **opens in your browser** when it starts (`-no-browser` turns that off). Chrome and Edge can **install** it as an app with its own window.

## Fixed

- Wiki links inside code (indented or fenced blocks, including in quotes and lists) and after a backslash are no longer treated as links, so renames leave code examples alone.
- Notes over 4 MiB are skipped without being read into memory. An oversized note stays in the trash, with a clear reason, instead of being restored.
- Preview no longer shows front matter as a heading, and note excerpts and word counts leave it out.
- Ticking a checklist box in Write works in Safari.

## Downloads

One archive for **Linux amd64** holds `coyotenote`, the README, the guide, the license and third-party notices. Check it against `SHA256SUMS`. `govulncheck` and `npm audit` report no known vulnerabilities.

[Full changelog: v0.5.9 → v0.6.0](https://github.com/eg36/Coyotenote/compare/v0.5.9...v0.6.0)
